user.title: Electricity price source
user.description: Select the entity that provides the dynamic electricity price forecast. Nordpool, EPEX Spot, ENTSO-E, aWATTar and hourly price arrays are detected automatically.

data.price_offset: Price offset (grid fees, taxes per kWh)
data.feed_in_tariff: Feed-in tariff (0 = market price; a fixed tariff below the spread never exports)

data_description.price_entity: Entity that exposes hourly electricity prices as an attribute list (e.g. sensor.nordpool_kwh_de_eur_3_10_025).
data_description.price_offset: Added to every market price. Typically covers grid fees, taxes and your supplier's margin (e.g. 0.12 EUR/kWh). Positive = more expensive.
data_description.feed_in_tariff: What you earn per kWh exported to the grid. 0 = dynamic market price. A fixed rate below the spread (default 0.20) will never trigger an export.

battery.title: Battery parameters
battery.description: Describe your home battery. The state of charge is read live from the selected entity.

data_description.soc_entity: Sensor reporting the current state of charge in percent (0-100). Example: sensor.byd_battery_box_premium_hv_state_of_charge.
data_description.capacity_kwh: Usable battery capacity in kWh, excluding the reserve SOC. Example for a BYD HVS 10: 10.2 kWh.
data_description.max_charge_power_w: Maximum charge power drawn from the grid, in watts. Typically 3000-5000 W.
data_description.max_discharge_power_w: Maximum discharge power, in watts. Typically 3000-5000 W.
data_description.min_soc: Lower state-of-charge bound in percent. The battery is never discharged below this. Recommended: 10 %.
data_description.max_soc: Upper state-of-charge bound in percent. The battery is never charged above this. Recommended: 95 %.
data_description.efficiency: Roundtrip efficiency in percent: kWh you get back divided by kWh you put in, times 100. Typically 85-95 %.
data_description.battery_charge_energy_entity: Optional meter for total charged kWh (total_increasing). Both meters together enable the actual-savings sensors. Example: sensor.battery_energy_charged.
data_description.battery_discharge_energy_entity: Optional meter for total discharged kWh (total_increasing). Both meters together enable the actual-savings sensors. Example: sensor.battery_energy_discharged.

control.title: Battery control scripts
control.description: Smart Battery Pilot controls your battery through Home Assistant scripts. Create one script per action for your inverter (see the documentation for vendor examples). The charge script receives the variable `power_w`.

data_description.script_charge: Called when the battery should charge from the grid. Receives the variable power_w (charge power in watts).
data_description.script_idle: Called when discharging should be blocked, so the battery keeps its energy for a more expensive hour.
data_description.script_auto: Returns the inverter to its normal self-consumption mode.
data_description.script_export: Optional: called when energy should be sold to the grid during very high prices.

consumption.title: Household consumption
consumption.description: Select the sensor measuring total house consumption (power in W or energy in kWh). It is used to learn your consumption profile from history.

data_description.consumption_entity: Total household consumption in W or kWh. Used to train the consumption profile.
data_description.temperature_entity: Optional: improves the consumption forecast for heat pump households by correlating with outdoor temperature.
data_description.has_heat_pump: Enables the heating-demand feature in the consumption forecast as soon as any temperature history exists, even a patchy one.

pv.title: PV forecast (optional)
pv.description: If you have solar, select daily production forecast sensors (kWh). Expected PV is subtracted from the consumption forecast.

data_description.pv_forecast_today: PV production forecast for today in kWh (e.g. Open-Meteo Solar Forecast or Solcast).
data_description.pv_forecast_tomorrow: PV production forecast for tomorrow in kWh - improves overnight planning considerably.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Current PV power. Shown as a live value on the Lovelace card.

error.unsupported_price_format: The price format of this entity was not recognized. See the documentation for supported integrations.
error.no_future_prices: The entity contains no future prices.
error.soc_range_invalid: Minimum SOC must be below maximum SOC.

data.training_days: History days used for consumption training

data_description.spread_threshold: Minimum price difference between charging and discharging, in EUR/kWh. Below this, arbitrage does not pay for the conversion losses. Recommended: 0.10-0.25 EUR/kWh.
data_description.discharge_mode: Self-consumption only: the battery covers your own demand. Self-consumption + export: also sells to the grid at very high prices (needs an export script).
data_description.training_days: Days of history used to train the consumption profile. More = steadier, but slower to follow a change in habits. Recommended: 30-60 days.
